patients.summary: Retired elementary school teacher with COPD who joins the practice in 2016, is diagnosed with osteoporosis in 2018, and then has pill esophagitis on alendronate, two T12 compression fractures, a left hip fracture, two C. difficile infections and, in 2026, an early-stage serous ovarian carcinoma treated surgically. No osteoporosis drug follows the alendronate.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
70 y/o retired elementary school teacher here to establish. Her previous internist retired this summer and a neighbor sent her our way. Brought a handwritten list.

PMH (per pt, records to follow):
- COPD. Told about four years ago after a breathing test at the old office. Gets winded on hills, otherwise fine. Never put on an inhaler. No hospital stays for her lungs.
- Knee arthritis; knees ache after gardening; takes OTC ibuprofen a couple of times a month. Not every week.
- Postmenopausal since 51. Never took hormones.

PSH: none. 3 vaginal deliveries.
Meds: multivitamin daily. Ibuprofen OTC occasional as above.
Allergies: NKDA.

FHx: mother broke her hip, told it was from thin bones. Father had COPD. Maternal grandmother died of ovarian cancer.

SHx: married, husband retired too. Three grown children, two in state. Former smoker, quit in her mid-50s. Glass of wine on a Saturday night, that's it. No regular exercise, walks the dog some. Eats well. No calcium or vitamin D.

ROS: no cough or sputum day to day. No chest pain. No GI complaints. Sleeps ok. Mood good.

Exam: vitals as charted. Pleasant, slim. HEENT unremarkable. Lungs with mildly decreased breath sounds at the bases, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart RRR, no murmur. Abdomen soft. Knees with bony enlargement and crepitus, full ROM, no effusion. No edema. Neuro grossly intact.

A/P
1. COPD by history, mild symptoms, no exacerbations. Will look at old spirometry when records come. No inhaler for now.
2. Knee OA. Occasional ibuprofen ok at this frequency, take with food.
3. Health maintenance: Tdap and Prevnar 13 today. PPSV23 next year. Flu shot once in stock. Labs today incl. lipids, TSH, hep C screen. Colonoscopy and mammograms were done at the old office, will confirm dates from records. Bone density: asked her to think about it, will bring up at her wellness visit.
4. Records release signed.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your recent lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mrs. McKenna, your blood work from last week came back fine. Kidney and liver tests, blood count, thyroid and cholesterol are all in the normal range, and the hepatitis C screen was negative. Nothing to change. See you in the spring.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: High-dose flu vaccine given IM left deltoid. Screening questions negative, no prior reactions. Tolerated well, VIS given.

reports.text: Outside pulmonary function study (prior practice, scanned). Pre-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC 0.66. FEV1 74% of predicted. FVC within normal limits. No significant change after bronchodilator. Effort and reproducibility acceptable.
reports.conclusion: Persistent airflow obstruction consistent with COPD, mild to moderate. No significant bronchodilator response.

documents.title: Records from Prior Primary Care Practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
58 pages received from prior internist's office, scanned to media.

PCP review of highlights:
- Spirometry 5/2014: obstruction, FEV1 74% predicted, ratio 0.66, no bronchodilator response. That's the COPD diagnosis.
- Colonoscopy 2013: normal to the terminal ileum, no polyps. Prior office recommended 10 years.
- Screening mammograms every other year, most recent 2015, all negative.
- Paps normal through her 60s, then stopped.
- No DXA on file.
- Med list there: multivitamin only. Allergies NKDA.
Nothing in here that changes the plan.

Reviewed old records with her: spirometry from 2014 confirms COPD. Colonoscopy 2013 normal.

COPD, stable, mild. Discussed an albuterol inhaler to have at home; she'd rather not, doesn't feel she needs it. Fine.
Knee OA, stable.

reports.text: Indication: postmenopausal screening; family history of hip fracture. Technique: DXA of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and left hip. Lumbar spine L1-L4 T-score -2.8. Left femoral neck T-score -2.6. Left total hip within the osteopenic range. No vertebrae excluded. No prior study for comparison.
reports.conclusion: Bone mineral density decreased at the lumbar spine and femoral neck, in the osteoporotic range by WHO criteria.

documents.title: Office Visit - Bone Density Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to go over the DXA and blood work.

She thinks she has gotten about 3 cm shorter over the last several years; her slacks are suddenly too long. Some mild low-to-mid back aching off and on, mostly after standing at the stove or a long walk with the dog, eases when she sits. Never fallen, never broken a bone. No night pain, no weight loss, no numbness or weakness in the legs.

Meds: multivitamin daily, nothing else regularly. No calcium, no vitamin D. Not much dairy.
Menopause at 51, no HRT. Former smoker. Wine about once a week. Not exercising beyond dog walks.
FHx: mother's osteoporotic hip fracture.

Exam: vitals as charted, height 157 cm today (158 cm at her first visit here). Thoracic kyphosis. Mild tenderness to percussion over the lower thoracic spine, no step-off. Lower extremity strength and reflexes normal. Gait steady.

Data: DXA 2/26 lumbar spine T -2.8, L femoral neck T -2.6. CMP, CBC, phosphorus, TSH all normal.

A/P
Osteoporosis, postmenopausal. Reviewed what the numbers mean and her fracture risk, especially with her mother's history.
- Start alendronate 70 mg weekly. Went over how to take it carefully: first thing in the morning, plain water, full glass, stay upright 30 min, nothing else by mouth for half an hour. Printed instructions given.
- Calcium carbonate 1250 mg twice daily with meals and vitamin D3 1000 units daily.
- Weight-bearing exercise; she'll look into the senior center's balance class.
- Back aching likely postural/mechanical with the kyphosis. Call if it becomes sharp or constant.
Follow up 3 months.

conditions.label: Pill-induced esophagitis

medications.drug: omeprazole 20 MG Delayed Release Oral Capsule
medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth daily 30 minutes before breakfast for 8 weeks

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 78. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST-segment or T-wave abnormality.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department and observation unit. Visit 4/23/2018 to 4/24/2018. Copy to primary care.

CC: pain with swallowing and behind the breastbone.

HPI: 72F with osteoporosis, COPD. Two days of abrupt-onset odynophagia with retrosternal pain, much worse getting solids down. Liquids tolerated. No travel, no sick contacts, nothing new in her diet. Takes alendronate once weekly (started last month) and uses ibuprofen as needed for knee osteoarthritis. No vomiting, no hematemesis, no melena. Pain is not exertional.

Meds: alendronate 70 mg weekly; calcium carbonate; vitamin D3; multivitamin; ibuprofen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, minimal wine. Retired teacher.
Family: mother osteoporotic hip fracture, father COPD, maternal grandmother ovarian cancer.

Exam: afebrile, VS within normal limits. Oropharynx clear without thrush or lesions. No cervical lymphadenopathy. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft and nontender.

Workup: CBC and BMP unremarkable. hs-troponin 3. ECG normal sinus rhythm without ischemic change.

Course: placed in observation; GI consulted for endoscopy in the morning, see separate report.

Diagnosis: pill-induced esophagitis, likely alendronate +/- NSAID.

Disposition: discharged 4/24. Stop alendronate. Stop ibuprofen; avoid NSAIDs. Omeprazole 20 mg daily for 8 weeks. Soft diet and cool liquids for several days. Take any pills upright with a full glass of water. PCP follow-up within 1 week; return for inability to swallow liquids, vomiting blood or black stools.

documents.title: Upper Endoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Procedure: esophagogastroduodenoscopy, 4/24/2018, regional hospital endoscopy suite, moderate sedation.
Indication: odynophagia and retrosternal pain after starting weekly alendronate.

Findings:
- Mid-esophagus: a single, localized, sharply demarcated ulcer with a clean base. No active or recent bleeding, no visible vessel. Surrounding mucosa otherwise normal. No stricture.
- Distal esophagus and GE junction normal. No hiatal hernia.
- Stomach normal.
- Duodenum normal to the second portion.

Impression: discrete mid-esophageal ulcer, appearance typical of pill injury.

Recommendations: discontinue alendronate and NSAIDs; PPI daily for 8 weeks; no repeat endoscopy needed if symptoms resolve.

documents.title: Post-ED call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Received ED and endoscopy records. Called pt: swallowing a little better, still sore with bread and meat, managing soups and yogurt. Taking omeprazole every morning. Has stopped the alendronate and the ibuprofen as told. Appt with PCP Tues 5/1.

Today swallowing is maybe 70% better. Soft foods fine, still a catch with dry toast. No vomiting, no black stools. On omeprazole daily. Off alendronate and ibuprofen.

She feels bad about it; she is fairly sure she took the alendronate correctly but admits she went back to bed for a bit after it on at least one Sunday. Reassured her.

Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

A/P
Pill esophagitis. Finish 8 weeks of omeprazole. Stay off NSAIDs.
Knees: acetaminophen in place of ibuprofen, up to 3 g a day.
Osteoporosis: alendronate stopped. Keep calcium and vitamin D. Recheck in about 8 weeks.

reports.text: Lateral view of the thoracolumbar spine. Wedge-shaped deformity of the T12 vertebral body with anterior height loss. Posterior vertebral body line preserved. No retropulsion. Remaining vertebral heights maintained. Diffuse osteopenia. Alignment otherwise normal.
reports.conclusion: Wedge compression deformity of T12, consistent with osteoporotic compression fracture.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department, 5/10/2019. Faxed to PCP.

CC: low back pain x 2 days.

HPI: 73-year-old woman with known osteoporosis, previously noted height loss and intermittent mechanical back aches. Two days ago she lifted a large pot full of water off the stove and felt a sharp pain low in her back. Constant since, sharp, stays in one place, no radiation into the legs. No fall or other trauma. No fever, no bowel or bladder incontinence, no weight loss.

PMH: osteoporosis; pill esophagitis 2018; COPD; postmenopausal.
Meds: calcium and vitamin D supplements; multivitamin; acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker (quit about 15 years ago), minimal alcohol, retired teacher.

Exam: VS stable. Point tenderness over the T12 spinous process. No bruising or swelling. Strength 5/5 in both legs, reflexes symmetric, sensation intact. Gait slow but steady.

Labs: calcium 9.8, phosphate 3.5, alk phos 70, 25-OH vitamin D 32.
Imaging: lateral spine film with a wedge deformity of T12.

Assessment: acute osteoporotic compression fracture T12, neurologically intact.

Plan: scheduled acetaminophen, tramadol 50 mg q6h prn severe pain (#20). Activity as tolerated, avoid lifting. Follow up with PCP this week.

documents.title: Post-ED call

documents.body: Pt called to let us know she was in the ED Friday, told she has a compression fracture in her back. Hurting but manageable with acetaminophen and the tramadol at bedtime. No leg weakness, no trouble with bladder. Records requested from the ED. Appt Thursday with PCP.

Pain 5/10 today, was 9 at its worst. Worse getting in and out of bed, better lying flat. Using acetaminophen every 6 hours and a tramadol at night only; tramadol makes her a little foggy so she's careful on the stairs. Bowels moving. No leg symptoms.

Exam: vitals as charted. Moves stiffly. Tender over T12. Strength and reflexes normal in the legs.

A/P
T12 osteoporotic compression fracture. Pain improving.
- Acetaminophen scheduled, tramadol sparingly, stop once she can.
- Log-roll out of bed; no lifting over a gallon of milk.
- Husband is doing the heavy work at home.
- Continue calcium and vitamin D.
Recheck in 3 months, call sooner if pain worsens or leg weakness.

Regional hospital emergency department, 7/24/2020.

CC: severe low back pain.

HPI: 74F, osteoporosis with a T12 compression fracture last year. This afternoon she picked up a heavy carton of canning jars and had immediate severe sharp pain in the middle of her low back. Does not travel down the legs. Denies trauma, fever, incontinence of bowel or bladder, or weight loss.

Meds: calcium, vitamin D, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.
Social: former smoker quit ~15 yrs, minimal alcohol, retired teacher.

Exam: vitals normal. Afebrile. Tender to palpation over T12. No neurological deficit; strength, sensation and reflexes normal. SLR negative both sides.

Labs: Ca 9.8, phos 3.5, alk phos 70, vitamin D 30. COVID PCR negative.
XR T and L spine: T12 compression fracture, more height loss than 2019.

Impression: acute osteoporotic T12 compression fracture, recurrent at the same level, neuro intact.

Plan: acetaminophen around the clock, tramadol prn (#15). Ice/heat. No lifting. Close PCP follow-up; consider outpatient options for her osteoporosis with PCP.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary - Orthopedic Surgery
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, orthopedic surgery service. Admitted 9/7/2021, discharged 9/11/2021 to a skilled nursing facility for rehabilitation.

Diagnosis: displaced left femoral neck fracture.
Procedure: left total hip arthroplasty, 9/8/2021.

History: 75-year-old woman with osteoporosis and two prior T12 compression fractures (2019, 2020). At home on 9/7 she caught her foot on a rug and fell straight onto her left side. Immediate severe left hip pain, unable to stand. No head strike, no loss of consciousness.
PMH: osteoporosis, COPD, postmenopausal, pill esophagitis (2018).
Home meds: calcium carbonate, vitamin D3, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, minimal alcohol, retired teacher, lives with husband.

Exam on arrival: left leg shortened and externally rotated. Could not bear weight on the left. Distal pulses and sensation intact.
Imaging: left hip radiographs show a displaced femoral neck fracture, with the cortical outline broken and an irregular lucent fracture line. Chest X-ray clear.
Pre-op labs unremarkable.

Course: medically cleared. Left total hip arthroplasty on hospital day 2 without complication. Perioperative cefazolin. Mobilized with PT on POD 1, weight bearing as tolerated with posterior hip precautions. Pain controlled. Voiding, bowels moving.

Discharge meds: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily to complete 28 days (last dose 10/6); oxycodone-acetaminophen 5/325 q6h prn severe pain; acetaminophen 500 mg prn mild pain (count toward daily acetaminophen total); calcium carbonate; vitamin D3; multivitamin.
Follow-up: orthopedics wound check and X-ray at 6 weeks; PCP after discharge from rehab. Recommend outpatient bone health follow-up with PCP.

No falls during stay.

Discharged home with home physical therapy 2 to 3 times weekly. Remaining enoxaparin through 10/6. PCP follow-up next week. Allergies NKDA.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary - Medicine
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital, medicine service. Admitted 11/19/2021, discharged home 11/23/2021.

Diagnosis: severe Clostridioides difficile infection, no toxic megacolon.

History: 75F, three days of watery diarrhea, crampy belly pain and low-grade fever. Hospitalized in September for a left hip fracture (total hip, then rehab). Has COPD and finished an oral antibiotic course for pneumonia about two and a half weeks ago.
Home meds: calcium carbonate, vitamin D3, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, minimal alcohol, retired teacher.
Family: mother osteoporotic hip fracture; father COPD; maternal grandmother ovarian cancer.

Admission vitals: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), BP 130/85, HR 92, RR 18.
Exam: mild LLQ tenderness without rebound or guarding; hyperactive bowel sounds; no peripheral edema; otherwise unremarkable. Healed L hip incision.
Labs: WBC 15,000, Hgb 13.2, platelets 250,000, creatinine 1.0, electrolytes normal. Stool C. difficile toxin positive (resulted 11/20).

Course: contact precautions, IV fluids, oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily from 11/19. Fever resolved by day 2, stools down to 2 to 3 a day and thickening by discharge. Tolerating diet. No abdominal distension; imaging not needed.

Discharge: complete oral vancomycin 125 mg QID for 10 days total (last dose 11/28). Avoid unnecessary antibiotics. Handwashing with soap and water, bleach cleaning of bathroom. PCP visit within 1 week.

documents.title: Transitional care call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called after discharge yesterday. Diarrhea slowing, 3 soft stools today, no fever. Taking vancomycin four times a day, last dose Sunday. Husband bleaching the bathroom. Drinking well. Appt next Tuesday.

conditions.label: Community-acquired pneumonia

documents.title: Post-Discharge Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Admitted 11/19 to 11/23 with severe C. diff after the pneumonia antibiotics. Discharge summary reviewed. RN call 11/24.

Finished oral vancomycin on Sunday. One or two soft stools a day now, formed this morning. No fever. Eating, but weight is down to 55 kg from about 58 last year. Tired. Cough from the pneumonia is gone, no albuterol use for two weeks.
Hip: walking with cane outdoors, none indoors. Ortho happy at 6 weeks.

Exam: vitals as charted. Thin, but looks better than I expected. Lungs clear, no crackles at R base. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds.

A/P
1. Severe C. difficile infection, completed vancomycin, improving. Watch for relapse; call for 3 or more loose stools a day. Antibiotics only if clearly needed.
2. Pneumonia, resolved clinically.
3. Weight loss after two hospital stays. Protein shakes between meals. Recheck weight in 6 weeks.
4. Hip arthroplasty, recovering well.
5. Osteoporosis on calcium and D.

documents.title: Follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Checked in after C. diff. Bowels normal, once a day, formed. No fever. Appetite good, drinking a shake every afternoon. Asked if she can get her flu shot now; yes, scheduled with nurse Thursday.

COPD exacerbation, increased dyspnea, sputum volume and purulence.

Call if no better in 3 days or worse sooner. If she gets diarrhea after this, call right away.

Regional hospital emergency department, 3/21/2022.

CC: diarrhea x3 days.

HPI: 76F with osteoporosis, COPD and C. difficile infection in November 2021. Three days of watery diarrhea, belly pain and low-grade fevers, 6 to 8 unformed stools a day. Finished doxycycline and prednisone for a COPD flare about two weeks ago. No blood in stool. Tolerating fluids.
PMH: osteoporosis with T12 fractures and L hip fracture s/p THA (2021); COPD; pill esophagitis; prior C. diff.
Meds: calcium, vitamin D3, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Social: former smoker, minimal alcohol, retired teacher.

Vitals: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), HR 102, BP 135/85.
Exam: dry mucous membranes. Abdomen soft, mild diffuse tenderness, no rebound or guarding, not distended. 

Labs: WBC 15,000. Creatinine normal. Stool positive for C. difficile toxin and GDH antigen.

Course: 1 L IV fluid, heart rate improved to 88. Tolerating PO. Discussed admission; patient prefers home, husband present, able to drink. Reasonable.

Assessment: second episode of C. difficile infection, severe by WBC criterion.
Plan: fidaxomicin 200 mg twice daily x10 days (first dose given here). Hydrate. Return for worsening pain, distension, inability to keep fluids down or lightheadedness. PCP follow-up within a week.

conditions.label: Postmenopausal bleeding

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Vaginal Bleeding
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One episode of vaginal bleeding on Saturday 2/28, came on suddenly, bright red, lasted part of the day. None since. No trauma or injury. No pelvic pain, no discharge, no urinary symptoms, no weight loss. Menopause at 51, no hormones ever. She is frightened by it; her grandmother had ovarian cancer.
Meds unchanged: calcium, vitamin D3, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn, albuterol prn.

Exam: vitals as charted. Abdomen soft, nontender, no mass. Deferred pelvic exam to gynecology at her preference, since she'll need an exam and ultrasound there anyway.

A/P
Postmenopausal bleeding, single episode. Needs endometrial evaluation. Urgent gynecology referral; staff called and got her in next week. I told her honestly that most often this turns out to be something benign, but it has to be looked at.
Call if bleeding recurs heavily, dizziness, or pain.

reports.text: Transabdominal and transvaginal pelvic ultrasound. Uterus anteverted, normal size for age, smooth contour. Endometrial stripe is thickened. Right ovary contains a 1.3 cm heterogeneous solid-appearing mass. Left ovary small and atrophic, unremarkable. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Thickened endometrial stripe in a postmenopausal patient. 1.3 cm heterogeneous right ovarian mass.

documents.title: Gynecology Consultation
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
Outside gynecology group. Visit 3/12/2026. Thank you for referring Mrs. McKenna.

Reason: postmenopausal bleeding.

HPI: 80-year-old woman with one abrupt episode of vaginal bleeding on 2/28 that upset her a good deal. No recent trauma. History of osteoporotic fractures (T12 twice, left hip). Menopause at 51, no HRT. G3P3, all vaginal deliveries. Mammograms every two years, all normal. Sexually active, monogamous with her husband of 55 years.
PMH: osteoporosis, COPD, prior pill esophagitis, C. difficile x2, L THA.
Meds: calcium, vitamin D, multivitamin, acetaminophen, albuterol prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: maternal grandmother with ovarian cancer; mother osteoporotic hip fracture; father COPD.

Exam: vitals normal. External genitalia atrophic, no lesions. Speculum: atrophic vaginal mucosa, cervix normal, no active bleeding. Bimanual: uterus small, nontender; no palpable adnexal mass.

Ultrasound today: thickened endometrial stripe; 1.3 cm heterogeneous mass in the right ovary.
CBC normal today.

Procedure: office endometrial biopsy with a Pipelle after verbal and written consent; tolerated well, scant tissue sent.
CA-125 drawn.

Assessment: postmenopausal bleeding with thickened endometrium and a small complex right ovarian mass.
Plan: await biopsy and CA-125. Given the solid-appearing ovarian lesion, referring to gynecologic oncology regardless of biopsy result. Will send results.

reports.text: Specimen: endometrium, office biopsy. Gross: scant fragments of tan tissue and blood. Microscopic: fragments of inactive endometrium with weakly formed glands in compact stroma. No hyperplasia. No atypia. No malignancy identified.
reports.conclusion: Inactive endometrium. Negative for hyperplasia and malignancy.

- Endometrial biopsy: inactive endometrium, no hyperplasia or cancer.

Discussed by phone with the patient. Because of the solid component in the 1.3 cm right ovarian mass she is scheduled with gynecologic oncology on 4/2. Please call with questions.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Consultation
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Regional cancer center, gynecologic oncology. Seen 4/2/2026. Copy to PCP.

Referred for a 1.3 cm heterogeneous right ovarian mass found on ultrasound during workup of a single episode of postmenopausal bleeding. Endometrial biopsy benign (inactive). CA-125 31.

Health: independent, active, walks daily. COPD without recent exacerbation. Osteoporosis with prior fractures and L THA. Two prior C. difficile infections, noted for perioperative antibiotic planning. NKDA. Former smoker.
Family: maternal grandmother ovarian cancer.

Exam: well appearing. Abdomen soft, no mass, no ascites. Pelvic: atrophic changes, no palpable adnexal mass. No inguinal or supraclavicular nodes.

Assessment: small solid-appearing right adnexal mass in a postmenopausal woman, indeterminate. Bleeding unexplained by biopsy.
Plan:
1. CT chest, abdomen and pelvis.
2. If no distant disease, laparoscopic hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, frozen section, and staging if malignant.
3. Anesthesia evaluation given COPD.
4. Genetic counseling after surgery depending on pathology.
Patient and husband agree.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Emphysematous changes in both upper lobes. No pulmonary nodule or mass. No pleural effusion. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary adenopathy. Heart normal size. Old T12 compression deformity, kyphosis.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease. Emphysema.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT abdomen and pelvis with oral and IV contrast. Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys unremarkable. No ascites. No peritoneal nodularity or omental thickening. No retroperitoneal or pelvic adenopathy. Uterus normal in size for age. 1.3 cm right adnexal lesion corresponding to the ultrasound finding. Left adnexa unremarkable. Left hip arthroplasty with streak artifact. Old T12 compression deformity.
reports.conclusion: 1.3 cm right adnexal lesion. No ascites, adenopathy or metastatic disease.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Gynecologic Oncology
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Regional cancer center. Admitted 4/28/2026 for planned surgery, discharged home 4/29/2026.

Procedure 4/28: robotic-assisted laparoscopic total hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, pelvic washings, infracolic omentectomy and bilateral pelvic lymph node sampling.
Findings: 1.3 cm firm lesion within the right ovary, capsule intact, ovarian surface smooth. No ascites. Peritoneal surfaces, diaphragm, bowel and omentum without visible disease. Uterus, left ovary and both tubes grossly normal. Frozen section of the right ovary: carcinoma, favor serous; staging completed as above.
EBL 50 mL. No complications.
Perioperative cefazolin single dose only, per her C. difficile history.

Course: ambulating evening of surgery, tolerating diet, voiding. Pain controlled with acetaminophen; no opioids needed after PACU.

Discharge: acetaminophen as needed. No lifting over 10 lb for 6 weeks. Resume calcium, vitamin D, multivitamin, albuterol prn. Final pathology to follow; post-op visit in 3 weeks.

conditions.label: Serous cystadenocarcinoma of ovary
conditions.note: Right ovary, low grade, 1.3 cm, FIGO stage IA

reports.text:
Specimens: uterus, cervix, bilateral tubes and ovaries; omentum; right and left pelvic lymph nodes; pelvic washings.
Right ovary: serous cystadenocarcinoma, low grade, 1.3 cm. Tumor confined to the ovary. Capsule intact. No ovarian surface involvement. No lymphovascular invasion identified.
Left ovary and both fallopian tubes: benign, no tumor.
Uterus and cervix: inactive endometrium; benign myometrium; cervix without dysplasia.
Omentum: no tumor.
Lymph nodes: 0 of 8 involved (right pelvic 0/4, left pelvic 0/4).
Pelvic washings: negative for malignant cells.
reports.conclusion: Low-grade serous cystadenocarcinoma of the right ovary, 1.3 cm, confined to the ovary with intact capsule. Washings and lymph nodes negative. Pathologic stage pT1a pN0, FIGO IA.

documents.title: Pathology received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Final path from gyn onc: low-grade serous carcinoma of R ovary, 1.3 cm, confined, nodes and washings negative, FIGO IA. Uterus benign. Gyn onc reviewed with her by phone today, per her message. Added to problem list. Will see her after her post-op visit.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Post-operative Visit
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Seen 5/19/2026, three weeks after laparoscopic hysterectomy, BSO and staging.

Recovering well. Port sites healed. Mild fatigue. Bowels and bladder normal. No vaginal bleeding.
Exam: incisions healed. Abdomen soft. Vaginal cuff intact on gentle exam.

Pathology reviewed with patient and husband: low-grade serous carcinoma of the right ovary, stage IA, completely removed.

Plan:
1. No adjuvant chemotherapy recommended for stage IA low-grade disease.
2. Surveillance: visit with exam and CA-125 every 3 months for the first 2 years; next in mid-August.
3. Germline genetic testing recommended for all ovarian cancers and with her grandmother's history; consented, sample sent today.
4. Resume normal activity; lifting restriction until 6 weeks.

documents.title: Germline Genetic Testing Report
documents.author: genetic counseling
documents.body:
Multigene hereditary cancer panel (including BRCA1, BRCA2, mismatch repair genes, RAD51C, RAD51D, BRIP1, PALB2 and others), blood sample collected 5/19/2026.
Result: NEGATIVE. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants identified. No variants of uncertain significance reported.
Interpretation: does not exclude hereditary risk entirely; family members' risk based on family history. Results discussed with the patient by the genetic counselor 6/2/2026.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, also first visit here since her surgery.

Interval: single episode of postmenopausal bleeding in Feb; gyn found thickened endometrium (biopsy benign) and a 1.3 cm R ovarian mass. CT no spread. 4/28 laparoscopic hysterectomy, BSO, staging: low-grade serous carcinoma of the right ovary, stage IA. No chemo. Germline panel negative. Gyn onc surveillance every 3 months, next in August. Records all reviewed.

How she's doing: energy nearly back. Weight 54, down a bit since surgery, eating well now. No bleeding, no pelvic pain, bowels normal. Back to the balance class last week. Walking daily. She says the hardest part was the waiting. Husband has been a rock.
PHQ-2 1 (a few low days in the spring), not depressed now.
Function: independent in ADLs and IADLs. No falls. Cognition intact.

Meds: calcium carbonate 1250 mg bid, vitamin D3 1000 units daily, multivitamin, acetaminophen prn, albuterol prn (rare).

Exam: vitals as charted. Thin, well. Kyphosis. Lungs distant, clear. Heart regular. Abdomen: healed port sites, soft, nontender. No edema.

A/P
1. Ovarian serous carcinoma, stage IA, s/p surgery. Surveillance with gyn onc.
2. Postmenopausal bleeding, resolved after hysterectomy.
3. COPD stable.
4. Osteoporosis: calcium and vitamin D. Fall prevention.
5. Knee OA.
6. Weight: protein with each meal; recheck in fall.
Prevention: flu and COVID at the October visit. Labs today.
RTC October.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Ruth, your labs from Monday all look normal: blood count, kidneys, liver, calcium, and vitamin D at 33. See you in October.

documents.title: October appointment
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, can my October appointment be in the morning? My husband has his own doctor visits in the afternoons that month. Thank you.

documents.title: RE: October appointment
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Ruth, you're now booked Tuesday, October 13 at 9:30 am, and we'll have your flu and COVID vaccines ready.

documents.title: Gynecologic Oncology Surveillance Visit
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Surveillance visit 8/18/2026, about 4 months after surgery for stage IA low-grade serous carcinoma of the right ovary.

Feels well. No abdominal bloating, pain, early satiety or vaginal bleeding. Weight stable.
Exam: no supraclavicular or inguinal adenopathy. Abdomen soft, no mass, no ascites. Pelvic: vaginal cuff well healed, no nodularity or mass.
CA-125: 14 U/mL.

Assessment: no evidence of disease.
Plan: next surveillance visit with CA-125 in 3 months (November).
